BENITEZ Mayor Bacolod City League of Cities of the Philippines - National Chairman Dear Hon. Benitez: 3 JUL v;traÅ This pertains to the letter dated 15 July 2024 requesting for this Departmen on on the status of LCP's leadership given the six-month preventive suspension of LCP National President and Cebu City Maylor Michael L. Rama. This Department opines that in the absence of any provision under the constitution and by- Laws of the leagues and federations of local elective officials as authorized under Section 509 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code (LGC), that will govern the situation, a preventive suspension imposed upon a local elective official will result in a temporary vacancy in the seat of the concerned official's position in the same league or federation. To resolve first the issue on whether there is a vacancy in the LCP, we refer for guidance to Sec. 500 of the LGC, which states: "Section 500. Representation. - Every city shall be represented in the league by the city mayor or in his absence, by the city vice-mayor or a sanggunian member duly elected for the purpose by the members, who shall attend all meetings and participate in the deliberations of the league. " The provision on "absence" is a recognition of the fact that membership in the LCP is grounded upon a person being a sitting Mayor. Stated otherwise, a city mayor under preventive suspension temporarily loses his representation as he could be deemed "absent" Likewise, Mayor Rama's preventive suspension will not result in Cebu City's lack of representation in the LCP considering that in the interim, Cebu City will be represented by the Vice-Mayor. We are also guided by the rationale behind the imposition of preventive suspension which is to avoid the concerned elective official's influence to the investigation or the proceedings being held in connection to his/her case; to protect the integrity of records and other evidence; and to that effect, to uphold an untainted and impartial resolution of cases. Common to all leagues and federations of local elective officials established under Sections 491, 496, 499 and 502, of the LGC, is the primary purpose of their organization which is ventilating, articulating and crystallizing issues affecting government administration of the political subdivisions and securing through proper and legal means, the solutions thereto. However, we cannot undermine the fact that this too is a venue of political connections between and among its members. Connections that are grounded on both personal and political idealism and interests. This is where we find the need to curtail the aspect of possible indirect influence a preventively suspended local elective official may have when he/she will retain his/her post as officer of the league/federation. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

From this respect the most logical inference the Department may arrive at is that the purpose and rationale behind the imposition of preventive suspension should extend to the position the concerned preventively suspended elective official is holding in the league/federation. To interpret otherwise is to run against the legislative intent behind Section 63 (b) of the Local Government Code. Having established the existence of temporary vacancy, we move on to the issue on succession. Per your submission, Section 5 of the League's Constitution and By-laws states that in case of absence, disability, death, or resignation of the National President, the Executive Vice- President (EVP) shall act as the National President. We opine that the same provision governs. The Executive Vice-President shall temporarily assume the duties of the National President of the League of Cities of the President consistent with Section 507, LGC, viz: Section 507. Constitution and By-laws of the Liga and the Leagues. - All other matters not herein otherwise provided for affecting the internal organization of the leagues of local government units shall be governed by their respective constitution and by-laws which are hereby made suppletory to the provision of this Chapter: Provided, That said Constitution and By-laws shall always conform to the provisions of the Constitution and existing laws. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concern. Thank you. Respectfully yours, THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . UAN CTOR R.
